successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance domain interface is exported from the balance module model file and exposes the attributes id, employeeId, leavePolicyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status, createdAt, updatedAt; status is typed as BalanceStatus imported from src/shared/types/index.ts.

The balance repository interface declares all five operations: findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId, leavePolicyId) returning Promise<LeaveBalance | null>, findByEmployee(employeeId) returning Promise<LeaveBalance[]>, create(Omit<LeaveBalance,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>) returning Promise<LeaveBalance>, update(id, Partial<LeaveBalance>) returning Promise<LeaveBalance | null>, and deductDays(id, days) returning Promise<LeaveBalance | null>.

The concrete repository class implements the balance repository interface and is constructible with no arguments (direct pool import from src/shared/db/connection.ts, no constructor injection); it persists and returns LeaveBalance rows for create, findByEmployeeAndPolicy, and findByEmployee.

deductDays performs a single atomic UPDATE that decrements remaining_days and increments used_days by the same day count in one statement with a RETURNING clause, returning the updated LeaveBalance or null when no row matches the id.

update builds a dynamic SET clause from the provided partial (only supplied fields, parameterized indices) and appends updated_at = NOW(); when the partial is empty it returns the current row without relying on a findById method (which the balance interface does not define); it returns null when no row matches the id.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/modules/balance/balance.repository.test.ts mock the shared db connection module, construct the repository with no args, and assert exact SQL strings and parameter arrays via toHaveBeenCalledWith for each operation including the atomic deductDays UPDATE...RETURNING; tests cover found, not-found (null), and database-failure (typed error) cases.
The new balance module files compile under strict TypeScript (tsc --noEmit) with no implicit any and no unused/missing imports, and the Jest suite passes.

constraints: Follow the policy repository pattern: direct import of pool from ../../shared/db/connection, no constructor injection, constructed with new PgLeaveBalanceRepository() (no args). Do NOT use the employee pattern (constructor-injected Pool, path-mapped imports).

All SQL must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, ...); no string-interpolated user input. This satisfies the no-direct-db-outside-repository and input-safety rules and matches the policy repository.

Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks. Use unknown with type guards for caught errors (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)) as the policy repository does; never use any.
Database access must go through the repository layer only (GP-001). The balance repository is the sole component that issues SQL against the leave_balances table; no inline SQL elsewhere.

Tests must mock the connection module (../../../../src/shared/db/connection) exporting __mockQuery, use relative imports, construct the repository with no args, and assert exact SQL via toHaveBeenCalledWith — mirroring the policy test pattern, not the employee test pattern.

Module dependency rule: the balance module may import only from shared-types and the shared db connection; it must not import internals of other modules (employee, policy, leave). Per ARCHITECTURE, balance depends on policy and shared-types only at the service layer, not in this data-layer phase.
outOfScope: Balance service, controller, and routes — this phase is the data layer only (model, repository interface, repository). Service orchestration and HTTP surface are later phases.

Audit logging (GP-002) for balance mutations — deductDays/update/create are repository-level persistence, not state-changing business operations requiring audit records; audit wiring belongs to the service/orchestration phase.
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) and API input validation (GP-003) — these apply at API boundaries; the repository has no HTTP surface in this phase.
Balance accrual logic, status transitions (ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED→FROZEN→CLOSED), and restore-on-cancellation — these are business rules for the service phase; the repository only persists and reads.
A findById method on the balance repository interface — explicitly omitted by the spec; update must handle the empty-partial case inline without delegating to findById.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveBalance is uniquely scoped per (employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear); the findByEmployeeAndPolicy lookup resolves a single balance or none, and the entity's remainingDays must equal totalEntitlement minus usedDays after any deductDays mutation (the atomic UPDATE preserves this relationship in one statement).

status is constrained to the BalanceStatus enum values (ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN, CLOSED) defined in src/shared/types/index.ts; the model types it as BalanceStatus and the repository maps the database status column back to that enum.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the matching LeaveBalance or null when no row matches; on database failure throws a typed Error whose message identifies the operation and the underlying cause.
Returns an array (possibly empty) of LeaveBalance rows for the employee; on database failure throws a typed Error identifying the operation and cause.

Inserts a new leave_balances row and returns the persisted LeaveBalance with generated id/createdAt/updatedAt; on constraint violation or database failure throws a typed Error identifying the operation and cause.

Applies only supplied fields via a dynamic parameterized SET clause with updated_at = NOW(); returns the updated LeaveBalance or null when no row matches the id; on database failure throws a typed Error identifying the operation and cause. The empty-partial case must not rely on a findById method.

Executes a single atomic UPDATE that decrements remaining_days and increments used_days by the same count with a RETURNING clause; returns the updated LeaveBalance or null when no row matches the id; on database failure throws a typed Error identifying the operation and cause. The decrement and increment must occur in one statement so the balance cannot be observed in an inconsistent intermediate state.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The balance repository must match the policy repository's structural conventions: direct `import { pool } from '../../shared/db/connection'`, no constructor injection, constructed with `new PgLeaveBalanceRepository()` (no args), try/catch with `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)` rethrown as a typed Error, and a private row-to-entity mapper.

The update method's dynamic SET-clause construction (parameterized indices, appended updated_at = NOW(), id as the final positional parameter) must follow the policy repository's update implementation, except the empty-partial branch must be self-contained (no findById delegation) since the balance interface omits findById.

The LeaveBalance model's status field and the repository's status mapping must use the BalanceStatus enum exported from src/shared/types/index.ts (ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN, CLOSED) — do not redefine or duplicate the enum.
The repository must obtain its pg Pool via the exported `pool` from src/shared/db/connection.ts (the same shared connection the policy repository uses); it must not instantiate its own Pool.

The balance repository test must mirror the policy test's mocking strategy: jest.mock on '../../../../src/shared/db/connection' exporting __mockQuery, relative imports of the repository and model, no-arg construction, and exact-SQL assertions via toHaveBeenCalledWith — not the employee test's pg-module mock or constructor-injection pattern.

integrationPoints.why: The repository executes all SQL through the shared pool export; this is the sole database integration for the balance data layer.
The LeaveBalance model and repository status mapping depend on the already-defined BalanceStatus enum; this phase consumes but does not modify it.

The repository persists against the leave_balances table whose columns (id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at) and FKs to employees/leave_policies define the row mapping the repository must satisfy.

Per PLAN.md Phase 6, the future LeaveService will call balanceRepository.deductDays() on approval; the deductDays atomic semantics established here are the contract that later orchestration relies on. This phase only defines the contract, not the wiring.
